knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of a Tangent Line of a Curve With Fractional Powers at a Given Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-6\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-6{x}^{1/2}) \\  & =3-6\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =3-\frac{3}{\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=25$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=25} & =3-\frac{3}{\sqrt{25}} \\  & =3-\frac{3}{5} \\  & =\frac{12}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at the point $(25,45)$ is

$$
m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=25}=\frac{12}{5}.
$$

This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\sqrt{x}-6{x}^{3/4}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{x}^{1/2}-6{x}^{3/4}) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}-6\cdot \frac{3}{4}{x}^{-1/4} \\  & =3{x}^{-1/2}-\frac{9}{2}{x}^{-1/4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=81$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=81} & =3\cdot \frac{1}{9}-\frac{9}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =-\frac{7}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at the point $(81,-108)$ is

$$
m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=81}=-\frac{7}{6}.
$$
